system_description.narrative_title: Middle East conflict disrupts global energy, shipping, and markets
system_description.narrative_summary: A widening Iran-centered conflict and proxy attacks (notably by Houthis and allied militias) are degrading Gulf energy infrastructure and maritime routes, triggering sharp oil and fuel price rises, shipping reroutes, and supply-chain strain. Treated as an open system, it comprises multiple state and non-state actors, critical infrastructure nodes (pipelines, Strait of Hormuz, ports), markets and logistics networks exchanging flows of energy, weapons, finance and information; damage to nodes produces reinforcing feedbacks—price spikes, political pressure, arms transfers, materiel shortfalls, and either further escalation or urgent diplomacy. These coupled dynamics are cascading into global markets, national budgets and domestic politics.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: Iran and its regional proxies (Houthis, militias), Gulf states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, Bahrain), US and allied military and diplomatic actors, critical energy infrastructure (East-West pipeline, pipelines bypassing Hormuz, terminals), maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, Suez Canal), global oil and refined product markets, shipping companies and insurers, defense supply chains (munitions, aircraft), national economies and household fuel consumers, and international institutions responding (UN, IAEA).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system and international energy-security architecture
adjacent_subsystems: International maritime trade & logistics (Red Sea, Suez, Hormuz)
US domestic politics & defense-industrial supply chain
Regional diplomacy and security architecture (Gulf states, UN actors)

variables.name: Energy export capacity
variables.description: Aggregate physical capacity to export crude oil and refined products via pipelines, terminals and tanker loadings.

variables.name: Maritime chokepoint accessibility
variables.description: Effective openness and transit throughput of major maritime chokepoints used for energy and trade flows.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure damage
variables.description: Extent of physical damage to energy and maritime infrastructure such as pipelines, refineries, terminals and port facilities.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting rate
variables.description: Rate at which commercial shipping alters established routes (percent or number of voyages rerouted per time unit).

variables.name: Fuel and oil price level
variables.description: Average market price level for crude oil and refined fuel products on global markets.

variables.name: Insurance premium and availability
variables.description: Cost and availability of marine, cargo and energy liability insurance coverage for shipments and facilities.

variables.name: Freight and shipping cost level
variables.description: Average freight and shipping cost levels for container, bulk and tanker transport on major routes.

variables.name: Supply chain lead time for energy inputs
variables.description: Average delivery lead times for fuel, refining inputs, spare parts and consumables needed by energy and transport sectors.

variables.name: Military force deployment intensity
variables.description: Aggregate operational presence and active deployment intensity of armed forces and security assets in the region.

variables.name: Arms and munitions inventory levels
variables.description: Aggregate stock levels of munitions, ordnance and other consumable military materiel available to combatants.

variables.name: Diplomatic tension level
variables.description: Degree of diplomatic hostility, sanctions, and breakdown in formal communication channels between actors.

variables.name: Conflict escalation pressure
variables.description: Intensity of ongoing processes (attacks, proxy operations, reprisals) that increase the probability of wider military escalation.

variables.name: Market volatility and risk premia
variables.description: Financial market volatility and risk premia associated with energy-security uncertainty and related asset-price swings.

variables.name: Household fuel affordability
variables.description: Share of household income required to purchase typical fuel and energy needs, reflecting consumer price pressure.

variables.name: Repair and restoration rate
variables.description: Rate at which damaged energy and maritime infrastructure is repaired and returned to operational service.

variables.name: Alternative export route capacity
variables.description: Aggregate capacity and utilization of alternative pipelines, land corridors and terminals that bypass primary maritime chokepoints.

catalysts.title: UN General Assembly week of meetings
catalysts.description: High-level UNGA meetings (world leaders, US-Gulf bilateral talks) likely to shape diplomatic backchannels and conflict de‑escalation efforts.
catalysts.rationale: ‘Why are world leaders at the UN next week’ and Trump plans meeting Gulf leaders at UN next week.

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi attacks and advances
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi targets, shipping and regional assets likely to continue, sustaining disruption to maritime flows and markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis strike Saudi targets anew', 'Houthi blitz leaves Saudi Arabia exposed', Houthi claims and Red Sea disruptions.

catalysts.title: Saudi pipeline outage & alternative export measures
catalysts.description: Saudi closure of East‑West pipeline and rapid shift to Oman loading and ship‑to‑ship transfers to keep exports flowing.
catalysts.rationale: ‘Saudi Arabia shuts East‑West pipeline…’, 'Saudi offers more crude via Oman loading', 'offers ship‑to‑ship crude transfers'.

catalysts.title: Planned US munitions sale to Israel
catalysts.description: US administration plans a $2.8bn munitions sale to Israel; Congressional pushback may affect timing and regional dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: ‘Trump administration plans $2.8 billion munitions sale to Israel’ and congressional opposition headlines.

catalysts.title: US clears way for large aircraft sale to Saudi Arabia
catalysts.description: US approval process advances for a $24.3bn military aircraft sale to Saudi Arabia, affecting regional capabilities and alliances.
catalysts.rationale: ‘US clears way for $24.3 billion military aircraft sale to Saudi Arabia’ (Reuters, 2026-09-17).

catalysts.title: Iran–Gulf talks on Strait of Hormuz security
catalysts.description: Diplomatic meetings between Iran and Gulf states (and third‑party mediation) aimed at a Hormuz security deal could alter transit risk.
catalysts.rationale: ‘Iran and Gulf states to meet in push for Hormuz deal’ and China presses Iran to rein in Houthis after Saudi appeal.

catalysts.title: Carriers reroute more ships via Suez/alternate corridors
catalysts.description: Major carriers increasingly route containerships through Suez/alternate corridors in response to Red Sea and Hormuz risk, altering freight and insurance dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: ‘Carriers Shift More Containerships…’, 'Maersk, Hapag‑Lloyd to sail more container ships through the Suez Canal'.

catalysts.title: Decision on extending UN peacekeepers in Lebanon
catalysts.description: Pending deliberations and votes on extending the UNIFIL/peacekeeper mandate will affect local force posture and risk of escalation in southern Lebanon.
catalysts.rationale: ‘Paris and Beirut push to extend UN peacekeepers’ mission’ and Paris hosts military leaders to weigh post‑UN mission.
